I can't recommend it, simply put, I can't. It's a game that doesn't stray from the formula of the first game, but that's exactly the problem: it doesn't break the mold, it doesn't introduce anything new, and it doesn't offer an enriching or refreshing experience. I also noticed other technical issues, such as the game being poorly optimized, there are FPS drops and crashes, and there are many things about this title that just don’t sit right with me. And for a game that wasn’t released recently, it’s almost disappointing that they haven’t fixed these issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report severe performance issues including stuttering, frame drops, and lag spikes, particularly when moving the mouse or playing on handheld devices like the Steam deck.

citations.review_text: It worked fine for a while, but I opened the game again recently and its literal so laggy its unplayable. I have perfectly fine frames walking back and forth, but whenever I turn my mouse it becomes a nauseating slide show. Please fix the performance Monomi Park, I loved the first game and just want to be able to play the second.

An unoptimized disappointment

First of all, If you have a high refresh rate monitor and like playing above 144fps don't buy this game because the games fps slider doesn't even go above 144fps which shows that the devs are out of touch people who probably have only played stardew valley and never played games at high refresh rate.

Second of all, the games optimization is actually non existent. I have an rtx 2060 that gets me about 165-200 fps on Doom Eternal (a very graphically beautiful game) while I'm not even getting 100fps on the LOWEST SETTINGS on this unoptimized slop of a game that has clay graphics.

Third of all, I loaded into the game today and I'm suddenly getting 10 fps spikes when I move my mouse around, thus making the game unplayable for me now.

Conclusion: This game is a disappointment to the legacy of Slime Rancher 1 and the devs put 0% of their budget into optimizing the game, put 20% into making a worthless unoptimized game engine and graphics that runs like dog poop instead of using Slime Racnchers 1 engine that ran fine and the other 80% of the budget is put into worthless decorations in the shop that no one will ever buy. This game is the epitome of matcha slurping glasses wearing stardew valley playing (no disrespect to stardew valley) girls who don't actually care about making a good game but care about making cutesy comfy thingies for other matcha girls to go crazy about while playing on 60fps because they don't care about performance just like how the developers don't.

Also, the characters in this game are uninteresting and annoying but the devs try so hard to make you care about them in those little interactions but let's be real we're all skipping whatever Granny Evelyn is saying because she and all the other character have nothing of substance to offer.

was excited to play but have never really had the chance as i get constant stuttering and lag spikes even when put into low settings. the first slime rancher runs perfect and i love it. i know its not the computer as i play many games that are more demanding without the issues i have had with this game. hopefully one day i will be able to expeience this game that i paid for but as of writing this i have not been able to really try it out as the issues really make it unplayable for me.

Id love to keep playing because the scenery is beautiful and i want to discover all the slimes and build a great ranch but it is SUPER laggy on steam deck despite is verified status. if you liked the first sr and a a PC, then i highly recommend this game. i just hope you don't have the experience i did.

UPDATE
I found that just by changing the proton version to 11.0 it runs great! Hope this helped!

This could, and should, have been an overhaul and DLC for the first game. 

It doesn't change enough to be worth a full release, along with being less stable and more annoying. It can't handle nearly as many entities as the first game.

The new ranch expansions are sprawling and too far apart, even further apart than the first game. The UI is a step down. The Vacpack is TERRIBLE, the stupid thing is so finnicky that it will stop working if you even think about moving your mouse while trying to do anything; if it doesn't think it can detect something within an inch of its end it just won't do anything at all no matter how many times you click and hold; it stops sucking once it thinks it has sucked up what you were looking at even if there's more stuff AND you keep holding; and it doesn't even always bother fully sucking up what it does detect - it's just awful. The update to how sleeping works is quite nice, though.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the ranch layout as sprawling and note that running between separated areas feels repetitive or annoying.

citations.review_text:
I played the original Slime Rancher a long time ago. But in comparison this game feels so pale and grindy.

The spark is just gone. I really enjoy the looks of this game, and the different kinds of slimes and places you can encounter. But the gameplay is so, so bland. And the mechanics are a literal copy 1 to 1 from the original game with no deviation or creativity. The devs should have tried new mechanics or just new things in general, but it's lacking.

A majority of your time in the game is going to be in the Ranch, just running around, gathering plorts through your slow vac-gun, selling them off, or stockpiling them until it gets to the right point to sell them. At some point, you'll have so many slimes to ranch it becomes stressful. You get teleporters later on in the game but running around to each area that you unlock as a part of your ranch is also just annoying, takes forever to get to places

I'm sure I can find something later on to reduce the grind, but the drones cost so much to build. Plus I don't think I have the patience to go gather a ton of materials around different places over and over again. It becomes repetitive.

This game can still be enjoyable! But if you don't like the same repetitive cycle similar to the first game, then it's not for you.

I'm not too far in but I'm liking it so far! The story is a bit weird, but that's maybe just because I haven't been focusing on it at all lmao. So far I still prefer the 1st game, but it's definitely fun and extremely pretty! I love all of the new slime designs they're so cute!! I kind of hate how sprawled out the ranch area is, I have to run around so much to get to everything and that's pretty annoying (I saw someone say that it felt like chore simulator and I think that's so funny- and also very true.)
I recommend it, but it definitely has flaws. (Honestly, for me it's worth it for the Angler Slimes!!!!🥺)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires significant resource grinding and material farming for gadgets, upgrades, and late-game content.

citations.review_text: came back to this game cus i started playing slime rancher 1, this game is fun, only problem is the all the grinding you gotta do for the gadgets.

I liked the first one, and I like this one. 

My one critique is that it feels a bit grindy. Lots of running around until you get a decent amount of resources and start to plan things out. It's not really intellectually demanding planning... moreso just managing your very, very limited hotbar. When I discover a new area, I kinda just want to do everything, but I don't think that's possible. You will have 3-4 of your inventory slots full of new science resources and the new slimes/food won't fit in the remaining slots. You will likely need 2-3 trips if you are going in blind or don't have links ready to go. Large, path blocking slimes take 1-2 slots of food to clear, taking even more slots or time to scavenge the local area for food.

Very heavy on the inventory management of it all. I'd prefer more slots to just play the game without as much backtracking.
fun but like really really really really grindy its actualyl maddening

I had to put the game down once i got to the "mid-end game" areas with the shadow plort portals. Its not fun to spend hours grinding these materials. You need perhaps a couple hundred to a thousand of them, which is really time consuming and unrewarding. If you miss a deposit place for them, good luck finding it without a wiki. 

The most annoying element of the game is material farming. In SR1 it was fine to create the drills to harvest the goods, but having to go out every day to grind honey or jellystone is annoying. The drones can be a nice tool for that, but then youre trading off using a hard to come by drone out in the wild for needing to do more ranch work in their absence, like manually harvesting hundreds of plorts. By the time you have enough drones to afford putting them out in the wild, you have pretty much beaten the game and only need to expand the sanctuary, so whats the point?

The Drones are really annoying at times. they feel like they harvest pretty slow on the range, and dont do enough to make it feel like the ranch is automated. Its annoying to craft them. I end up having to spend so much time grinding honey for just another one. Maybe thats just me though.

I like the 1.2 addition of the sanctuary. It probably is the best part of the game. I like that making a pretty enclosure for slimes is rewarded. The only issue with the space is that the sprinkles are so annoying to farm, and drones are wayyy too slow to harvest them. It is also super annoying to find the shiny slimes, but i know thats by design. 

Frankly the story is pretty mid. Pretty much only one new character is in the game, with the cast from the old game staying in touch. The story line just feels a bit nonsensical and handwavy, and ends with a really boring and unrewarding "boss fight." I wish there was more flesh to the story and more people to meet. What happened to the fun mini games like the first game had with the quicksilver slimes? 

Overall, I do not like the grindy elemen…

citations.review_text: They removed the rad, quantum, mosaic, quicksilver and glitch slimes :( Otherwise a 9/10 game would and did play again.

Like Slimerancher but a bit longer and a little worse in some ways (in my opinion).

Also they removed two of my three favorite slimes :(

very joyous and whimsy! I love this game, if you liked the first one I'd highly reccomend it, it feels like the first game on a larger scale with the lab mechanics more integrated into the gameplay instead of off to the side. The lighting and colors are lovely, it just took some time for my eyes to adjust to the change in brightness and vibrancy from the first game. I very much enjoy being able to place gadgets anywhere to do shenanigans, and being able to buy decorations is really nice to have. Fire slimes are a lot less volatile in this one too, so I didn't have to worry about them dying if left unattended for too long, and the yolky slimes are super cute! yayayayaya this game is great, my only complaints are that you can't buy specific slime toys easily, you have to wait for the one you want to show up in the shop, and that they left out fashion pods, color customization, rad slimes, mosaic slimes, quantum slimes, and quicksilver slimes, otherwise great game!

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players enjoy the expanded map despite confusing navigation features.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the main dungeon area is confusing to navigate and the map features are unhelpful.

citations.review_text:
If you want a cozy, low stakes, pleasant experience I can't recommend it enough. The world is huge, there are so many new slimes, the automation is great now too.

The thing I love most about 2 compared to 1, is that they improved SO MUCH about the experience. You can play however you feel like. Hate grinding resources? Set up a drone and collect them passively while you decorate. Hate backtracking to portals to get around? Invest in transporters. You can put them anywhere and there's a ton of them. The economy feels way more balanced than it was in early access, there's always valuable things to spend money on. You can also get drones pretty early on. Theres a device that points you directly to resources if you need it. 
Lots of small tweaks that improve the game a lot, from the first game and the early access. Its worth going back to if you didn't vibe with the early access.

I really enjoy the gameplay loop of farm maintenance vs exploring. Although the main 'dungeon' of the game can be really confusing at times, and the shadow plort things are a pain without the upgrade. If you don't like exploring and just want to farm, completing the main story will probably frustrate you. Even with the portable tranporters.

Main negatives after playing a save for 100 hours: the vaccum speed when fully upgraded to 100 is soo freaking slow, I wish there was a faster way to move around large numbers of items. Wish there were more natural warp points in the labyrinth. Would love if there were different types of corrals, big or small, even temp ones you can place anywhere. 

Overall, a huge improvement from slime rancher 1 in every way.

I have hundreds of games. This one is the most frustrating I have ever played. The Grey Labyrinth is a nightmare. The map is absolutely useless. You can spend hours lost looking for areas you need to return to. The marker seems like a nice feature, but again  useless in the end. Unless you are the type that remembers exactly where every room is and how to get there, find another game. This one is migraine inducing.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a larger map and more areas to explore compared to the first game.

citations.review_text: I highly recommend this game to people who have played the previous Sime Rancher game. It is so lovable and packed with stuff to do! It has great graphics and world building, and has a much much bigger map to explore than the first game. I love how there are hundreds of slime largos and you can decorate almost anywhere what ever you want.

Genuinely such an incredible game <3

The fact that the game just keeps going and going with dozens of areas to explore and discover just blew me away. I seriously felt like I was exploring a whole new world with so much to offer. Not to mention the amount of love, details, and charm oozing from every area, especially late game. This game will always hold a special place in my heart, just as the first <3
